To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the behavioral expression and the intensity of the sickness response to lipopolisaccharides (LPS) depend on the priority of behavior under consideration.
the sickness behavior induced by LPS in lactating mice is differentially expressed depending on the behavioral priority of the tested behavior.
the behavioral effects of LPS are not uniform and that the expression of the sickness behavior depends on the priority that a behavior has in the behavioral hierarchy of a mouse.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential effects of LPS on maternal behavior in lactating mice and shows that the expression of sickness behavior depends on the priority that the behavior under consideration has.
the effects of LPS on maternal behavior and the possible role of the cytokines in the regulation of maternal behavior.
the behavioral effects of cytokines on lactating mothers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LPS-induced sickness in lactating mice is not a global depression of all maternal activities but rather a selective depression of the least essential maternal behavior, that is, nest building.
LPS-induced sickness does not prevent the mother from taking care of her young but rather induces a change in the way maternal behavior is expressed.
the sickness response to LPS does not affect the maternal behavior as a whole but rather the expression of the different components of the behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the priority of the maternal behavior, i.e., nest building versus pup retrieving, determines the behavioral expression of the sickness induced by LPS.
LPS-treated mothers are able to maintain their maternal behavior but at a cost of reduced nest building.
the priority of the pup-retrieving activity is higher than that of nest building in lactating mice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the behavioral effects of proinflammatory cytokine are not necessarily deleterious to the mother and her young.
the behavioral expression and the intensity of the sickness syndrome depend not only on the type of cytokine but also on the priority of a given behavior.
the behavioral expression in response to LPS is not a simple all-or-none response.
